(New Orleans, Louisiana) | college = * [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]] (2016–2017) * [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] (2018–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}} | team1 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]] | team2 = →[[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] | years3 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2022]] | team3 = [[Texas Legends]] | years4 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team4 = [[Capital City Go-Go]] | years5 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team5 = [[Memphis Hustle]] | years6 = {{nbay|2023|end}} | team6 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | years7 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team7 = Memphis Hustle | years8 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team8 = Memphis Grizzlies | highlights = * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2021) * AAC Defensive Player of the Year (2021) * AAC Sixth Man of the Year (2019) }} '''DeJon Jarmond Jarreau''' (born January 23, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player, who most recently played for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass Minutemen]] and the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]]. ==Early life and high school career== Jarreau grew up in the [[7th Ward of New Orleans]], a neighborhood suffering from crime and poverty.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Duarte|title=DeJon Jarreau's journey from New Orleans' Seventh Ward to University of Houston degree|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/DeJon-Jarreau-s-journey-from-New-Orleans-15816734.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=March 1, 2021}} He attended [[McDonogh 35 College Preparatory Charter High School]] in New Orleans.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Lopez|title=McDonogh 35 point guard De'Jon Jarreau top player in Louisiana according to Rivals|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/article_9cf8b007-c394-5512-a1d6-fafd7fa7ac38.html|work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]]|date=April 9, 2015|access-date=March 1, 2021}} He competed for Elfrid Payton Elite on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web|first=Josh|last=Preston|title=McDonogh 35's DeJon Jarreau competes in first ever Nike Basketball Academy: AAU Report|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/article_5cbc3c0a-48f8-5393-9efd-b19992051456.html|work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]]|date=June 30, 2015|access-date=March 1, 2021}} Jarreau was a four-star recruit and committed to playing college basketball for [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]] over an offer from [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]].{{cite web|first=Daniel|last=Malone|title=DeJon Jarreau, Brison Gresham pick UMass: Highly-touted NOLA duo commits to Minutemen over Miami|url=https://www.masslive.com/umassbasketball/2015/09/dejon_jarreau_brison_gresham_c.html|work=[[The Republican (Springfield, Massachusetts)|The Republican]]|date=September 28, 2015|access-date=March 1, 2021}} ==College career== On November 14, 2016, Jarreau recorded a freshman season-high 25 points, eight rebounds and six assists in a 90–88 loss to [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Vautour|title=Notebook: UMass DeJon Jarreau living up to advanced billing|url=https://www.gazettenet.com/UMass-DeJon-Jarreau-living-up-to-advanced-billing-6219363|work=[[Daily Hampshire Gazette]]|date=November 17, 2016|access-date=March 1, 2021}} He averaged 9.8 points and 4.5 assists per game. Jarreau left UMass after head coach [[Derek Kellogg]] was fired.{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Hewitt|title=DeJon Jarreau, Brison Gresham to transfer from UMass|url=https://www.bostonherald.com/2017/04/19/dejon-jarreau-brison-gresham-to-transfer-from-umass/|work=[[Boston Herald]]|date=April 19, 2017|access-date=June 23, 2021}} For his sophomore season, Jarreau transferred to [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]].{{cite web|first=Nathan|last=Brown|title=Houston's 'dynamic duo' made it from New Orleans to Sweet 16, 'a blessing' despite hardships|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/article_5e0787c3-912e-5918-a73b-5303d178f58b.html|work=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]]|date=March 28, 2019|access-date=March 1, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 8.7 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game and was named [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Duarte|title=UH's DeJon Jarreau goes back to sixth-man role|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/cougars/article/UH-s-DeJon-Jarreau-goes-back-to-sixth-man-role-14924643.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=December 21, 2019|access-date=March 1, 2021}} On February 1, 2020, he was ejected from a game against [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] for biting the leg of an opposing player and received a one-game suspension.{{cite web|first=Jenna|last=West|title=Houston's DeJon Jarreau Suspended for One Game After Biting Opponent's Leg|url=https://www.si.com/college/2020/02/02/dejon-jarreau-bites-opponent-leg-suspension-houston|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=February 2, 2020|access-date=March 1, 2021}} In his junior season, Jarreau averaged nine points, 4.3 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game. He declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] before withdrawing his name and returning to college.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Duarte|title=DeJon Jarreau returns to UH with more focus|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/DeJon-Jarreau-returns-to-UH-with-more-focus-15760444.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=November 28, 2020|access-date=March 1, 2021}} On March 12, 2021, Jarreau recorded 15 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 77–52 win over [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]] at the [[2021 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] quarterfinals. It was the first [[triple-double]] by a Houston player since [[Bo Outlaw]] in 1993 and the first in AAC Tournament history.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Duarte|title=DeJon Jarreau's triple-double powers UH's win over Tulane in AAC tournament|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/DeJon-Jarreau-s-triple-double-powers-UH-s-win-16022606.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=March 12, 2021|access-date=March 18, 2021}} As a senior, Jarreau averaged 10.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.3 steals per game.{{cite news|first=Justin|last=Quinn|title=Ex-Houston guard DeJon Jarreau reportedly conducting pre-draft workouts with Celtics|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2021/06/10/nba-boston-celtics-jarreau-predraft-workout/|work=Celtics Wire|date=June 10, 1021|access-date=June 23, 2021}} He was named AAC Defensive Player of the Year as well as Second Team All-AAC.{{cite web|title=American Athletic Conference Announces Men's Basketball Honors|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2021/3/9/american-athletic-conference-announces-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|website=TheAmerican.org|publisher=American Athletic Conference|date=March 10, 2021|access-date=March 10, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers / Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], he joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]]. Following a strong Summer League performance, he was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]] on August 24, 2021. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Pacers and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Jarreau to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-jarreau-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 24, 2021|access-date=August 25, 2021}} On December 15, he was waived after playing just one minute of one game for the Pacers.{{cite web|title=Pacers Waive Jarreau, Sign Taylor to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-jarreau-sign-taylor-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}} ===Texas Legends (2022) === On December 27, 2021, Jarreau's rights were traded by the [[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] to the [[Texas Legends]] in exchange for [[Kenny Williams (basketball, born 1996)|Kenny Williams]] and a 2022 first-round draft pick.{{cite web|title=Legends Acquire DeJon Jarreau|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-dejon-jarreau/|website=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2021|access-date=January 25, 2022}} On December 28, 2021, Jarreau signed a 10-day contract with the [[Houston Rockets]], via the hardship exemption.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=DuBose|title=Rockets add former University of Houston star DeJon Jarreau on hardship deal|url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2021/12/28/rockets-add-former-university-of-houston-star-dejon-jarreau-on-hardship-deal/|work=Rockets Wire|date=December 28, 2021|access-date=December 28, 2021}} On December 30, however, he entered the NBA's health and safety protocols and never played a game for the Rockets.{{cite web|title=Rockets' DeJon Jarreau: Lands in protocols|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-dejon-jarreau-lands-in-protocols/|website=CBSSports.com|date=December 30, 2021|access-date=January 7, 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220107184850/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-dejon-jarreau-lands-in-protocols/|archive-date=January 7, 2022}} After his contract with the Rockets expired, Jarreau rejoined the Legends. ===Capital City Go-Go (2022–2023)=== On January 23, 2022, Jarreau and a 2022 second-round draft pick were traded to the [[Capital City Go-Go]] in exchange for two 2022 first-round draft picks.{{cite web|title=CAPITAL CITY ACQUIRES DEJON JARREAU IN TRADE WITH TEXAS|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/capital-city-acquires-dejon-jarreau-in-trade-with-texas/|website=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2022|access-date=January 25, 2022}} On March 7, he was waived.{{cite web|title=2021-22 Capital City Go-Go Transactions|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction_History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 27, 2022}} On February 24, 2023, Jarreau was reacquired by the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 24, 2023}} ===Memphis Hustle (2023–2024)=== On December 26, 2023, Jarreau was traded to the [[Memphis Hustle]] in exchange for [[Mychal Mulder]]{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle acquire DeJon Jarreau from Capital City Go-Go|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-acquire-dejon-jarreau-from-capital-city-go-go|website=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2023|access-date=January 10, 2024}} and on March 10, 2024, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Dejon Jarreau to 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-dejon-jarreau-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 10, 2024|access-date=March 10, 2024}} Ten days later, he signed a second 10-day deal with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Dejon Jarreau and Maozinha Pereira to 10-day contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-dejon-jarreau-and-maozinha-pereira-to-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=March 20, 2024|access-date=March 20, 2024}} On March 30, he returned to the Hustle.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Memphis Hustle Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Memphis-Hustle/52/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 31, 2024}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2026)=== On March 13, 2026, Jarreau was signed to another 10-day contract with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|title=NBA Transactions|url=https://www.nba.com/players/transactions?TeamID=1610612763|website=NBA.com|date=March 13, 2026|access-date=March 18, 2026}} That night, Jarreau played 24 minutes and acquired six points, seven rebounds, and three assists against the [[2025–26 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]]. The following night, Jarreau put up 5-5-6 in 23 minutes against the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|title=NBA Transactions|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/schedule|website=NBA.com/Grizzlies|date=March 13, 2026|access-date=March 18, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== life== Dejon has a brother named John Jarreau. He is also the cousin of rapper [[Young Greatness]], who was shot and killed in 2018.{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Duarte|title=Dark cloud starting to lift for UH's grieving DeJon Jarreau|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/cougars/article/Dark-cloud-starting-to-lift-for-UH-s-grieving-13511370.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=January 5, 2019|access-date=March 1, 2021}} Jarreau was a basketball teammate of his close friend Brison Gresham in high school and college.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Baldwin|title=Life, Death and Buckets in The Big Easy — How Houston's DeJon Jarreau and Brison Gresham Became Brothers in Every Way That Matters|url=https://www.papercitymag.com/culture/houston-basketball-dejon-jarreau-brison-gresham-new-orleans-life-death/|work=PaperCity Magazine|date=March 24, 2019|access-date=March 1, 2021}} He was the first member of his family to graduate from college. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://umassathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dejon-jarreau/6987 UMass Minutemen bio] *[https://uhcougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dejon-jarreau/5901 Houston Cougars bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Jarreau, DeJon}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from New Orleans]] [[Category:Capital City Go-Go players]] [[Category:Fort Wayne Mad Ants players]] [[Category:Houston Cougars men's basketball players]] [[Category:Indiana Pacers players]] [[Category:Memphis Grizzlies players]] [[Category:Memphis Hustle players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Texas Legends players]] [[Category:UMass Minutemen basketball players]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:United States men's national basketball team players]]
